subject: Two-panel figure possible when using grid.text()?

messages.author: 7c1e3896b587548f
messages.subject: Two-panel figure possible when using grid.text()?
parts:
I've created two similar figures which both involve the following:

1) a straightforward ggplot() object, where my X axis represents time
2) two or three lines of text below the object, set to match the breaks on the X axis and indicate the number of patients for whom we have information at that point (N at risk)

My code for each figure resembles this:

plot.object <- ggplot(data = ...) ## plus all additional ggplot2 code

pdf(...)
print(plot.object, vp = viewport(...))
grid.text(...)
dev.off()

I need to put these figures into one file for manuscript publication, laid out in two rows by one column. I've used other information from this group to do the same for other figures, using "helper functions" which incorporate grid.layout() and viewport(); however, the use of grid.text() is not cooperating with that method (at least, not in any way that I can figure out). Is there a way to do this? Or a way to add the text below the X axis from within the ggplot statements?

Thanks so much for any help. My knowledge of grid graphics is obviously not strong enough to figure this out on my own!

- Jennifer Thompson

messages.author: e3f5ae2bbb1140ed
messages.subject: Re: Two-panel figure possible when using grid.text()?
parts:
Hi Jennifer
To place two or more ggplot2 plots on the same page, please using the
following code.

## layout function
vplayout <- function(x,y) {
viewport(layout.pos.row=x, layout.pos.col=y)
}


pdf(file="blah.pdf", width=8.5, height=11)
grid.newpage()
pushViewport(viewport(layout=grid.layout(2,1))) # two rows, one column

print(plot1, vp=vplayout(1,1))
print(plot2, vp=vplayout(2,1))
dev.off()

where plot1 and plot2 are the results of ggplot commands. You can use
svg, tiff, png, and jpeg to export your plot to a file.

All the best
Emilio

below the plot (sounds like Kaplan-Meier survival curves, which have a
defined lower limit of 0), you can use geom_text with a small negative y
value. You can end up with something like
